toolChanges.reason: Replaced by ESLint9 (ESLint 8 is deprecated on Codacy); all ESLint8 security concerns that fired (object injection, non-literal RegExp, unhandled async errors) are covered by the ESLint9 equivalents
Current ESLint engine; adds eslint-plugin-regexp ReDoS detection and sonarjs hardcoded-secrets checks on top of the ESLint8 coverage

Repo has no dependency manifests or lockfiles (third-party libs are vendored minified files that are already excluded); secret scanning remains covered by Biome noSecrets, ESLint9 sonarjs/no-hardcoded-secrets and Semgrep generic secret rules
IaC scanner; repository contains no Terraform/CloudFormation/Kubernetes/Docker files. Secret concerns covered by other tools
6 default ECMAScript best-practice/error-prone rules (ConsistentReturn, EqualComparison, UseBaseWithParseInt...). Runs on Cloud only (not supported on Windows locally)

patternChanges.reason: Environment mismatch: 114/114 hits are browser/WebExtension globals (chrome x84, document, URL, window, self, importScripts, setTimeout). Codacy exposes no globals/env parameter for this rule, so every hit is a false positive. Replaces ESLint8_no-undef (86 local / 71 Cloud issues)
Deduplicated: all 7 hits are intentionally unused `catch (_e)` bindings. Biome_lint_correctness_noUnusedVariables stays enabled, covers the same concern and honours the underscore-prefix convention
Deduplicated: fires on exactly the same 3 lines as ESLint9_security_detect-non-literal-regexp (kept)
Deduplicated: same finding as ESLint9_regexp_no-super-linear-move (kept — more precise, reports the attack string)
Wrong framework (Salesforce Lightning Web Components); innerHTML/XSS concern covered by Semgrep insecure-innerhtml and insecure-document-method

Deduplicated: Cloud shows it firing on the same 3 lines as ESLint9_security_detect-non-literal-regexp (kept, because ESLint also runs locally); ReDoS proper remains covered by Semgrep detect-redos and ESLint9 regexp rules
Wrong stack — React; project is a vanilla-JS browser extension
Wrong stack — Electron; project is a browser extension
Wrong stack — AWS IAM/S3 policies, Java Spring and TypeScript are not present in the repo
Noise floor: 88% of broad-config issues were High/Error, so low-severity CodeStyle rules were cut (8 Info-level hits)
Lizard was enabled with no patterns before; enabled complexity rules and set CCN threshold to 15 (Codacy's documented default) so only genuinely complex functions are flagged (CCN 16 and 31)
Function length check; flags one 80-line function in background.js

deduplication: Non-literal RegExp: kept ESLint9_security_detect-non-literal-regexp; disabled ESLint9_security-node_non-literal-reg-expr, Semgrep_javascript_dos_rule-non-literal-regexp and Semgrep detect-non-literal-regexp (identical findings)
Super-linear regex: kept ESLint9_regexp_no-super-linear-move; disabled ESLint9_sonarjs_slow-regex
innerHTML/XSS: kept Semgrep insecure-innerhtml + insecure-document-method; disabled ESLint9_@lwc_lwc_no-inner-html (LWC-specific)
newCoverage: Biome_lint_security_noSecrets (High, 1 issue — likely false positive on an i18n key, triage on Cloud)
Semgrep expanded from 34 to 422 patterns (JS security + generic secrets), Cloud-only on this machine
noisyButKept: ESLint9_security_detect-object-injection (13 issues) — known to be false-positive prone for `obj[key]` access, kept per security guardrail; triage individually on Cloud

keyImprovements: Local issues cut from 109 to 25 (-77%) while enabled patterns grew from 351 to 972 — every remaining issue is a security or complexity finding worth reviewing
Removed 86 `no-undef` false positives caused by the linter not knowing WebExtension/browser globals (chrome, document, URL...)
Migrated from deprecated ESLint 8 to ESLint 9, adding precise ReDoS detection (eslint-plugin-regexp) and hardcoded-secret checks
Deduplicated overlapping regex and innerHTML rules across ESLint, Semgrep and Biome so each finding is reported once
Lizard complexity checks now active (previously enabled with zero patterns), flagging the two genuinely complex functions (CCN 16 and 31)
Dropped Checkov and Trivy, which had nothing to scan in this repo (no IaC, no dependency manifests)
